# SOURCE: wordfreq English, top 50,000 words

- URL: https://pypi.org/project/wordfreq/3.1.1/ (wheel https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/24/61/62835c475d69872d30689f284497853fe33fe1d6dd18f57346d13305861d/wordfreq-3.1.1-py3-none-any.whl), source https://github.com/rspeer/wordfreq
- Fetched: 2026-11-14.
- Licence: code Apache-2.0; the data files "may be redistributed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 license (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)" (wordfreq README). Keep this folder separate, with this note. Upstream attributions required by the README: Google Books Ngrams (acknowledge, link http://books.google.com/ngrams), Leeds Internet Corpus, Wikipedia, ParaCrawl, OPUS OpenSubtitles 2018 (attribution to OpenSubtitles), SUBTLEX word lists (credit Marc Brysbaert et al.; SUBTLEX must stay clearly freely available data), and Twitter statistics (no content republished). Author: Robyn Speer.
- Subset: `en-top50k.tsv`, the first 50,000 entries of the `large_en` wordlist (wordfreq's merged English frequency list), decoded from `large_en.msgpack.gz` with a small own msgpack reader. Columns: `rank` (order by frequency bucket; order inside one bucket is arbitrary), `word`, `centibel` (wordfreq bucket value cB; frequency = 10^(-cB/100)), `zipf` (= 9 - cB/100), `band` (our own cut: very-common zipf>=6, common >=5, familiar >=4, uncommon >=3, rare below).
